Maya: Hey @Chris quick question 

Maya: Our custody agreement switches physical custody to me on June 1 (we did 50/50 until May). Im switching to Redwoods plan next month. Can our kid be covered on both of our employer plans at the same time or does one of us have to be primary? 
Chris: I was under the impression only one parent can carry a child as a dependent on employer coverage. The court order says primary residence with Maya starting June 1 but we split weekends. What docs do People Ops need to make the switch?
Owen (People Ops): Hi @Maya + @Chris  short answer: typically only one employer plan is primary for a dependent. If the court order names primary custody, that determines primary insurer. For joint custody without a clear assignment, we follow standard tiebreakers (parent with earlier birthday in the year, then custody percentage). Well need documentation to change coverage: custody/order PDF, proof of childs address (mail, school), and a completed Dual-Coverage Intent form.
BenefitsBot: KB: https://redwood.example.com/kb/benefits/dual-coverage-coordination  lists acceptable docs and COB rules.
Lina (Benefits): Steps to resolve this cleanly:
1) Upload the custody order or court decree (PDF).
2) Upload one proof of child's residence (school letter, utility, lease) showing the address where they will primarily live after 6/1.
3) If both of you already enrolled the child, complete the Dual Coverage Intent form (portal link).
4) Well open a COB case and confirm which plan is primary. If court order specifies coverage assignment, well follow that.
Maya: Thanks. If we switch primary mid-year, how will premiums/proration and claims be handled? I dont want either of us to get stuck with unpaid claims.
Owen (People Ops): Good Q. If the effective primary date is the court order date (e.g., 6/1) and you provide docs within 30 days, Benefits can process coverage changes retro to that date. Premium refunds/charges are handled via Payroll: refunds usually show up as a payroll credit within 1-2 pay cycles after Benefits confirms. Claims already paid will be adjusted by carriers via COB; you may see coordination recoveries or reimbursements.
Chris: Ugh I already added them on my Redwood enrollment during open enrollment. Is that a problem? Will claims be denied or delayed?
Lina (Benefits): Not ideal but common. If your plan is initially primary we'll coordinate claims with the other carrier when we switch primary. Claims shouldn't be denied outright; they may pend during COB. Upload the custody docs and we'll mark the duplicate dependent and set the proper primary. We can also generate a user-facing note you can show providers if billing questions arise.
Maya: Uploading custody decree and the school enrollment letter now. Also want to add the kid to dental under my plan while medical stays under Chris temporarily  possible?
Owen (People Ops): Yes, different carriers and benefit types can be split between parents (medical w/ Chris, dental w/ Maya) if both carriers allow it. Provide the carrier IDs and well coordinate primary for each benefit type.
Lina (Benefits): Case created #BP-11234. Well review docs within 3 business days and email both of you with the confirmed primary and any retro premium impact. If we need signatures from both parents for the Dual-Coverage Intent form well route that via the portal. :white_check_mark:
Chris: Appreciate it, Ill wait for the confirmation email.
Maya: Thanks everyone  saved me a headache.
